subject: Technical next steps: SDK onboarding, auth options, and routing policy draft
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Chen <anna@lexihealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed technical action items

Anna — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps to get you into a sandbox next week. Please flag anything missing.

Summary of asks from the call:
- SDK setup: LexiHealth wants a quick start with server-side SDK (Node + Python) and a browser-safe flow for client-side embeddings.
- Auth: procurement asked about API key rotation and a potential mTLS option.
- Routing / policies: you want latency-sensitive routing for conversational queries and a cheaper batch path for background summarization.
- Structured output / tool calling: prototypes discussed for appointment-booking and a small reranker for candidate responses.
- Embeddings & reranker: retention and PII considerations were called out.

Proposed technical action items (owner in parentheses):
1) Share an "integration checklist" with step-by-step SDK install and sample auth flows (I will attach v0). (Mina)
2) Provide two auth patterns: API key + rotation script, and a scoped mTLS reference for VPC installs; include security notes for SOC2 customers. (Aditya)
3) Draft routing policy: latency threshold (p90 < 180ms) -> primary route to rwd-llm-8g, fallback to rwd-llm-4q for high cost jobs; region routing: us-east primary, eu-west fallback. (Vanessa)
4) Sample structured-output schema and example function/tool manifest for appointment booking. (Ben)
5) Clarify embeddings retention options (short-term cache vs persistent index) and recommended reranker: redwood-rank-lite. (Mina)

Attachments: integration checklist + initial routing-policy YAML draft + MVP diagram.

Next steps: if this looks good, can we confirm a sandbox target date for next Tuesday (6/13)? Also please send any procurement constraints (PO terms, DPA comments) so Ben/Aditya can prep.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: lex ihealth-integration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), routing-policy-draft-v1.yaml (yaml), mvp-integration-diagram.pdf (pdf)

From: Anna Chen <anna@lexihealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LexiHealth Procurement <procurement@lexihealth.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jun 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed technical action items

Thanks Mina — this is great, really helpful to see the checklist. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) Sandbox timing: 6/13 works for our dev lead (we'll need a single API key and a short-lived client token for embeddings in the browser).
2) Auth: Procurement would prefer mTLS for any production VPC connection; for the sandbox we are ok with API keys but need a rotation cadence and audit logs. Does your dedicated/private offer provide KMS integrations?
3) Embeddings retention: our legal team asks that any embeddings derived from PHI be stored only in our own index — we can do local vector DB hosting, but we'd like to understand the export/import flow for embeddings and any server-side caching TTLs.
4) Routing: the latency thresholds you proposed sound reasonable; one follow-up: can we bind a cost cap per hour for background summarization jobs so we don't accidentally exceed budget during long re-index runs?

Also looping in procurement — our PO lead is Rachel (procurement@lexihealth.com). She'll share the standard PO and DPA.

—Anna
Anna Chen
Head of Product
LexiHealth

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed technical action items — sandbox link + checklist

Anna — + follow-up from our engineering side and a short checklist for Tuesday's sandbox session. See inline where we've assigned owners.

On auth and KMS:
- Aditya: "We support customer KMS integrations for Private; for Hosted we provide envelope encryption and customer-provided keys via our KMS connector. I'll attach an mTLS reference and a rotation script for API keys."

Routing policy (draft highlights) — Vanessa:
- Primary route: rwd-llm-8g (low-latency conversational) for queries where p50 < 120ms expected.
- Mid-tier fallback: rwd-llm-4q (quantized) when queue depth increases or cost threshold hits.
- Batch path: rwd-emb-batch for asynchronous summarization and nightly re-indexes (cost-optimized).
- Cost guardrails: soft hourly cap + alerting; recommend Dedicated pool for strict spend caps and burst isolation.

Embeddings & reranker notes — Mina:
- For PHI: recommend local vector DB (we'll provide export tooling). Sandbox default TTL: 24h cache on server; persistent index only when you run the import step.
- Reranker suggestion: redwood-rank-lite (low-cost reranker) for top-k reordering; for high accuracy we can enable redwood-rank-pro with slightly higher latency.

Sandbox checklist for 6/13 session:
1) Provision dev account + API key (Ben)
2) Walkthrough of Node SDK quickstart and browser token flow (Mina)
3) Show mTLS reference and KMS options (Aditya)
4) Load a small dataset for embeddings and demonstrate export/import (Mina)
5) Validate routing policy behavior by running a synthetic conversational load and a batch job (Vanessa)

Links / artifacts attached: integration checklist, routing-policy-draft-v1.yaml, and an MVP diagram. I've also posted a short runbook in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Clexi-integration

If that all looks good I'll schedule a 60-minute sandbox handoff for Tue 6/13 at 10:00am PT.

Best,
Mina
